If this Google dependency caught you off guard you simply did not do enough due diligence. This has always been the core risk. I spelled it out before, 58% to 69% of traffic historically came from search, management flagged it on the Q4 call last year, and the October removal of deep search access was a clear warning. None of this is new.

What did we actually get yesterday. Revenue up 53% to $895M and ahead of estimates. Earnings at $1.40 also a beat. Net income margin 32%. Free cash flow $363M at a 41% margin. Yes search referrals fell meaningfully in Q3 and Huffman said it was down more than 1M per week on average in October because of AI Overviews and AI Mode. And yes total daily uniques came in at 130.3M versus 133.7M expected with US down 2%. But the more important piece is logged in and app users, who drive more than 80% of monetization, still grew sequentially. US logged in held up while the bleed was in logged out. Q4 guidance at $1B to $1.03B is below the $1.05B analyst estimates but it is still in the same ballpark for 38% to 42% growth.

The bigger problem for me is not the traffic drop, it is that Huffman did not lay out how this conversion to a logged in only experience is actually going to work. The plan is to start with small AB tests in select international markets in Q4 to figure out prompts and tradeoffs. That creates uncertainty and the market hates uncertainty.
